يَا عِبَادِي، كُلُّكُمْ ضَالٌّ إِلَّا مَنْ هَدَيْتُهُ، فَاسْتَهْدُونِي أَهْدِكُمْ.

يَا عِبَادِي، كُلُّكُمْ جَائِعٌ إِلَّا مَنْ أَطْعَمْتُهُ، فَاسْتَطْعِمُونِي أُطْعِمْكُمْ.

يَا عِبَادِي، كُلُّكُمْ عَارٍ إِلَّا مَنْ كَسَوْتُهُ، فَاسْتَكْسُونِي أَكْسُكُمْ.

يَا عِبَادِي، إِنَّكُمْ تُخْطِئُونَ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، وَأَنَا أَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا، فَاسْتَغْفِرُونِي أَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ.

يَا عِبَادِي، إِنَّكُمْ لَنْ تَبْلُغُوا ضَرِّي فَتَضُرُّونِي، وَلَنْ تَبْلُغُوا نَفْعِي فَتَنْفَعُونِي.

يَا عِبَادِي، لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ، وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ، كَانُوا عَلَى أَتْقَى قَلْبِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ مِنْكُمْ، مَا زَادَ ذَلِكَ فِي مُلْكِي شَيْئًا.

5907 — Abū Dharr reported from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning what he narrated from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that He said:

“O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another.

O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I guide, so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you.

O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so ask Me for food and I will feed you.

O My servants, all of you are unclothed except those whom I clothe, so ask Me for clothing and I will clothe you.

O My servants, you commit sins by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you.

O My servants, you can never attain the ability to harm Me so as to harm Me, nor can you attain the ability to benefit Me so as to benefit Me.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the human beings among you and the jinn among you, were all as righteous as the most righteous heart of one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in the least.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the human beings among you and the jinn among you, were all as wicked as the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not diminish My dominion in the least.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the human beings among you and the jinn among you, all stood together on one plain and asked of Me, and I gave every person what he asked for, that would diminish what I possess no more than a needle diminishes the sea when it is dipped into it.

O My servants, they are only your deeds. I record them for you and then repay you for them in full. Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself.”

Saʿīd said: Whenever Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī narrated this hadith, he would kneel upon his knees.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2577).

5907 — Abū Dharr reported from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning what he narrated from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that He said:

“O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another.

O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I guide, so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you.

O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so ask Me for food and I will feed you.

O My servants, all of you are unclothed except those whom I clothe, so ask Me for clothing and I will clothe you.

O My servants, you commit sins by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you.

O My servants, you can never attain the ability to harm Me so as to harm Me, nor can you attain the ability to benefit Me so as to benefit Me.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the human beings among you and the jinn among you, were all as righteous as the most righteous heart of one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in the least.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the human beings among you and the jinn among you, were all as wicked as the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not diminish My dominion in the least.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the human beings among you and the jinn among you, all stood together on one plain and asked of Me, and I gave every person what he asked for, that would diminish what I possess no more than a needle diminishes the sea when it is dipped into it.

O My servants, they are only your deeds. I record them for you and then repay you for them in full. Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself.”

Saʿīd said: Whenever Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī narrated this hadith, he would kneel upon his knees.

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2577).

5911 — Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: “Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. Beware of obscenity, for Allah does not love obscenity or shameless conduct. Beware of greed, for greed is what destroyed those before you. It commanded them to be miserly, so they became miserly.” Then a man said: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which form of Islam is best? As for the desert-dweller, he responds when called and obeys when commanded. As for the town-dweller, his trial is greater of the two, and his reward is greater of the two.”

Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (6837), authenticated by Ibn Hibban (5176), and al-Hakim (1/11).

٥٩٢٠ — عن وائل بن حجر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( من غَصَبَ رجلاً أرضاً ظلماً، لقيَ اللّهَ وهو عليه غضبانُ)).

حسن: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (١٨/٢٢).

فقه الحديث:

ويكون حساب كل واحد حسب جريمته، فمنهم من يطوق به مثله من الأرض، ومنهم من يحاسب بحمل ترابها إلى المحشر، ومنهم من يحاسب بدخوله النار، ومنهم من يحاسب بغضب اللّٰه عليه، والنبي ﷺ بين هذه الأشكال من الجزاء في أوقات مختلفة.

5920 — Wa’il ibn Hujr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: “Whoever usurps a man’s land unjustly will meet Allah while He is angry with him.”

Hasan: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (22/18).

5924 — Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: “Do you know who the bankrupt one is?” They said: The bankrupt among us is the one who has neither money nor goods. So this one will be given from his good deeds, and that one will be given from his good deeds. If his good deeds run out before what he owes is settled, some of their sins will be taken and cast upon him, then he will be thrown into the Fire.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2581).

5925 — Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: “Rights will surely be returned to their owners on the Day of Resurrection, until retaliation will be taken for the hornless sheep against the horned sheep.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2582).

The hornless sheep is the one with no horns. The retaliation between the horned and hornless sheep is not a matter of moral accountability, because animals are not legally accountable; rather, it is a form of exact compensation. It clearly shows that animals will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and this is indicated by the verse: “And when the wild beasts are gathered.” [Surat al-Takwir: 5]

But the scholars said that being gathered on the Day of Resurrection does not necessarily mean reward, punishment, or moral accountability. Al-Nawawi mentioned this briefly. It also shows Allah’s power: if He gathers animals on the Day of Resurrection, even though they are not morally accountable, then how could He not gather human beings?

5926 — Abdullah reported from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Satan has despaired of idols being worshipped in the land of the Arabs, but he will be content from you with lesser things, and they are the destructive sins on the Day of Resurrection. Avoid injustices as much as you can, for a servant will come on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds, thinking they will save him. Then one servant after another will stand and say: My Lord, Your servant wronged me. So it will be said: Wipe away from his good deeds. This will continue until not a single good deed remains for him because of those sins. The likeness of that is like travelers who stopped in a barren land with no firewood. The people dispersed to gather wood, and before long they had gathered enough, made a great fire, and cooked what they wished. That is how sins are.”

Hasan: Narrated by Abu Ya‘la (5122) and Ahmad (3818).

5929 — Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said, “Help your brother whether he is a wrongdoer or one who has been wronged.” They said: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we understand helping him when he is wronged, but how do we help him when he is the wrongdoer? He said, “By restraining his hands.”

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2444).

٥٩٣٠ — عن جابر قال: اقتتل غلامان: غلام من المهاجرين، وغلام من الأنصار، فنادى المهاجر أو المهاجرون: يا للمهاجرين. ونادى الأنصاري: يا للأنصار. فخرج رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقال:

(( ما هذا دعوى أهل الجاهلية )). قالوا: لا، يا رسول اللّٰه إلا أن غلامين اقتتلا، فكسع أحدهما الآخر.

قال: (( فلا بأس، ولينصر الرجل أخاه ظالما أو مظلوما، إن كان ظالما فلينهه؛ فإنه له نصر، وإن كان مظلوما فلينصره )).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٨٤).

وقوله: (( كسع )) أي ضرب دبره. وقوله: (( فلا بأس )) معناه لم يحصل من هذه القصة بأس مما كنت خفتُه.

5930 — Jabir said: Two boys fought, one from the Emigrants and one from the Helpers. The Emigrant, or the Emigrants, called out, “O Emigrants!” and the Helper called out, “O Helpers!” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, came out and said: “What is this call of the people of the age of ignorance?” They said: Nothing, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, except that two boys fought and one of them struck the other on his backside. He said: “There is no harm, but let a man help his brother whether he is a wrongdoer or one who has been wronged. If he is a wrongdoer, then let him stop him, for that is helping him. And if he is wronged, then let him support him.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2584).

His saying, “kas‘a,” means he struck his backside. And his saying, “There is no harm,” means that nothing harmful resulted from this incident of the kind I had feared.

٥٩٣١ — عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:

«انْصُرْ أَخَاكَ ظَالِمًا أَوْ مَظْلُومًا».

قيل:

يا رسول الله، هذا نصره مظلومًا، فكيف نصره ظالمًا؟

قال:

«تُمْسِكُهُ مِنَ الظُّلْمِ، فَذَاكَ نَصْرُكَ إِيَّاهُ».

حسن: رواه ابن حبان في صحيحه (٥١٦٦).

٥٩٣٢ — عن البراء قال: أمرنا النبي ﷺ بسبع، ونهانا عن سبع: أمرنا باتباع الجنائز، وعيادة المريض، وإجابة الداعي، ونصر المظلوم، وإبرار القسم، ورد السلام، وتشميت العاطس. ونهانا عن سبع: آنية الفضة، وخاتم الذهب، والحرير، والديباج، والقسي، والإستبرق.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٢٣٩)، ومسلم (٢٠٦٦). واللفظ للبخاري.

والسابع عنده هو (( المياثر ))، وهو جمع ميثرة - بكسر الميم -، وهو وطاء كانت النساء يصنعنه لأزواجهن على السروج، وكان من مراكب العجم، ويكون من الحرير، ويكون من الصوف وغيره، فإذا كان من الحرير فيكون منهيا عنه.

(( والقسي )) - بفتح القاف - هي ثياب مضلعة بالحرير، تعمل بالقس، وهو موضع ببلاد مصر.

5932 — Al-Bara’ said: The Prophet ﷺ, commanded us with seven things and forbade us from seven things. He commanded us to follow funeral processions, visit the sick, respond to invitations, support the oppressed, fulfill oaths, return greetings of peace, and say “May Allah have mercy on you” to the one who sneezes. And he forbade us from seven things: silver vessels, gold rings, silk, brocade, qassiyy cloth, and istabraq.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1239) and Muslim (2066). The wording is that of al-Bukhari.

The seventh item in his version is “al-mayathir,” the plural of “mitharah,” with a kasrah on the mim. It is a cushion women used to make for their husbands on saddles, and it was from the riding gear of the non-Arabs. It could be made of silk, or of wool and other materials. If it was made of silk, then it was prohibited.

And “al-qassiyy,” with a fathah on the qaf, are garments striped with silk, made in al-Qass, a place in Egypt.

5933 — Thabit, the freedman of Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman, said: When the dispute occurred between Abdullah ibn Amr and Anbasah ibn Abi Sufyan, they prepared themselves for fighting. Khalid ibn al-As rode to Abdullah ibn Amr and admonished him. Abdullah ibn Amr said: Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said, “Whoever is killed defending his wealth is a martyr”?

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (141), and this is his wording. Also narrated by al-Bukhari (2480).

5934 — Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: “Whoever swears a binding oath in order to seize the wealth of a Muslim while he is sinful in that oath will meet Allah while He is angry with him.” Then al-Ash‘ath ibn Qays entered and said: What is Abu Abd al-Rahman narrating to you? They said: Such-and-such. He said: Abu Abd al-Rahman has spoken the truth. It was concerning me that this was revealed. There was a dispute between me and another man over land in Yemen, and I took the matter to the Prophet, ﷺ. He said: “Do you have proof?” I said: No. He said: “Then his oath.” I said: Then he will simply swear. At that point the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: “Whoever swears a binding oath to seize the wealth of a Muslim while he is sinful in it will meet Allah while He is angry with him.” Then the verse was revealed: “Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price…” [Aal Imran: 77] to the end of the verse.

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2356) and Muslim (138). The wording is that of Muslim.

In a narration in al-Bukhari (2516): “Your two witnesses, or else his oath.”

5936 — Abu Umamah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: “Whoever seizes the right of a Muslim by means of his oath, Allah has made the Fire obligatory for him and has forbidden Paradise for him.” A man said: Even if it is something small, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: “Even if it is a twig from an arak tree.”

Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (137).

«لَا جَلَبَ، وَلَا جَنَبَ، وَلَا شِغَارَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ، وَمَنِ انْتَهَبَ نُهْبَةً فَلَيْسَ مِنَّا».

٥٩٣٩ — عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( إن أبغض الرجال إلى اللّٰه الألد الخصم )).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤٥٧)، ومسلم (٢٦٦٨).

وقوله: (( الألد )) بمعنى شديد الخصومة، مأخوذ من لديدي الوادي، وهما جانباه، لأنه كلما احتج عليه بحجة أخذ في جانب آخر.

5939 — Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: “Indeed, the most hated of men to Allah is the stubborn, fiercely argumentative opponent.”

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2457) and Muslim (2668).

His saying, “al-aladd,” means one who is severe in argument and dispute. It is taken from the two sides of a valley, because whenever a proof is brought against him, he turns to another side.
